chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said:

A dispute arose between two men from the sons of my uncle regarding inheritance, so I advised them to write a letter to him regarding that so they might derive his view. So they both wrote to him together: 'May Allah make us your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who left her husband and her daughter and her mother?' And I said: 'May I be your ransom, if you see fit to answer us, answer us with the bitterness of the truth.'

So a letter came out to them both: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah grant us and you good health, with the best of health. I understood your letter wherein you mentioned that a woman died and left her husband and her daughter and her sister from her father and her mother. So the prescribed share is for the husband one-quarter, and whatever remains is for the daughter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a husband and daughter when the deceased woman's mother and sister are also alive?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of Quranic inheritance rules through a specific legal query sent to the Imam, highlighting the exclusion of the mother and sister when a husband and daughter are present. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise calculation of shares based on the presence of specific heirs, demonstrating how the Imam’s ruling aligns with the Quranic verses on fractional shares.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Al Ashary who said,

‘There occurred a dispute among two men from the sons of my uncle regarding inheritance. So I advised them to write a letter to him<sup>asws</sup> with regards to that in order to acquire his<sup>asws</sup> view. 
So they both wrote to him together, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make us to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a woman who left her husband and her daughter of her father and her mother?’ And I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! If you<sup>asws</sup> give your<sup>asws</sup> view, answer us with the bitterness of the truth’.

So there came out a letter to them both: ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Grant us<sup>asws</sup> and you good health, with the best of health. I understood your letter wherein you mentioned that a woman died and left her husband, and her daughter, and her sister from her father and her mother. So the Obligation (legislated shares of inheritance) is – for the husband is the one-quarter, and whatever remains is for the daughter’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Ash‘ariy who has narrated the following: “A dispute took place between two men of the sons of my uncle on a legacy.

I pointed out for them to write to him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it to find out his opinion in the matter. They wrote, ‘We pray to Allah to keep our souls in service for your cause, what do you say about the case of a woman who leaves behind her husband and her daughter from her father and mother?’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if you consider it proper answer us with the bitter truth.’

A letter came to them that said, “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah grant you and us good health and the best form. I understood your letter in which you have mentioned that a woman has left behind her husband, her daughter and a sister from her both parents. The ordained share of the husband is one-fourth and the rest belongs to the daughter.’”
